title: Johnsi Amalarani vs S.Arul Prakash on 19 July, 2016

paragraphs.text:
BEFORE THE MADURAI BENCH OF MADRAS HIGH COURT 

DATED : 19.07.2016 

CORAM 
THE HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE K.KALYANASUNDARAM 

TR.C.M.P.(MD).No.333 of 2016 
and 
C.M.P.(MD)No.6334 of 2016 


Johnsi Amalarani ... Petitioner/Respondent

 Vs.

S.Arul Prakash ... Respondent/Petitioner


PRAYER : Transfer Civil Miscellaneous Petition is filed under Section 24
of Civil Procedure Code, to withdraw and transfer the I.D.O.P.No.25 of 2016
from the file of the learned District and Sessions Judge, Tiruchirappalli and
transfer the same to the District and Sessions Court, Sivagangai be tried
along with I.D.O.P.No.23 of 2015 on his file.

!For Petitioner : Mr.P. Mahendran
^For Respondent : No appearance. 

:O R D E R

This Transfer Civil Miscellaneous Petition has been filed to withdraw
the application in I.D.O.P.No.25 of 2016 from the file of the learned
District and Sessions Judge, Thiruchirappalli and transfer the same to the
District and Sessions Court, Sivagangai to be tried along with I.D.O.P.No.23
of 2015.

2. Mr.P.Mahendran, learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that
the petitioner is the wife of the respondent and she is a permanent resident
of Karaikudi. The marriage between the petitioner and the respondent was
solemnized on 11.11.2012, as per the Christian Rites and Customs.

3. It is further submitted that earlier, the respondent filed
I.D.O.P.No.103 of 2013 before the III Additional District and Sessions Court,
Thiruchirappalli against the petitioner for restitution of conjugal rights
and the same was transferred from the III Additional District and Sessions
Court, Thiruchirappalli to the District and Sessions Court, Sivagangai in
Tr.C.M.P.No.74 of 2014 filed by the petitioner. While so, the respondent has
now filed I.D.O.P.No.25 of 2016 before the District and Sessions Court,
Thiruchirappalli under Section 10(VII) , 10(IX) and 10(X) of Indian Divorce
Act.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioner would further submit that the
petitioner has been blessed with twins and both of them are in the custody of
the petitioner, that after the petitioner left from the matrimonial house due
to harassment met by her, she is now residing with her aged parents and she
could not travel for more than 80 Kilometers to defend the case filed by her
husband.

5. Despite service of notice, the respondent has not chosen to appear
either in person or through counsel and contest the petition.

6. It is settled law and in the cases arise out matrimonial disputes,
the convenience of the wife shall be given preference.

7. In such view of the matter, this petition is allowed and the
petition in I.D.O.P.No.25 of 2016 is ordered to be withdrawn from the file of
the learned District and Sessions Judge, Thiruchirappalli and transferred to
the file of the District and Sessions Court, Sivagangai for joint trial along
with I.D.O.P.No.23 of 2015.

8. The learned District and Sessions Judge, Thiruchirappalli is
directed to transmit the entire records to the file of the learned District
and Sessions Judge, Sivagangai for joint trial along with I.D.O.P.No.23 of
2015, within a period of two weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this
order and the learned District and Sessions Judge, Sivagangai, after
obtaining the records on transfer, is directed to dispose the matter as
expeditiously as possible. No order as to costs. Consequently, connected
Miscellaneous Petition is closed.
1. The District and Sessions Court, Tiruchirappalli.
2. The District and Sessions Court, Sivagangai. .
